transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because I've been having a lot of trouble with my eating lately. What really scares me is that once I start eating... especially when I’m alone in the kitchen, it feels like I’ve just stepped aside. I can’t make myself stop. Even though I’m telling myself the whole time, ‘Janet, put it away,’ I just keep going. It's gotten to the point where I knew I needed to talk to someone about it.
After one of these episodes where you feel you can't stop eating, do you ever do anything afterward to try to make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never made myself throw up or used laxatives or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise a lot. Usually, I just... I just sit there feeling really miserable and full, and guilty about what I just did. But no, I don't do anything to try to undo it.
How often would you say these episodes of feeling out of control while eating happen, and how long has this been going on?

Well, when I look back at my kitchen calendar, and kind of track it by my food bank weeks... I'd say these episodes have been happening most weeks. Usually it's once or twice a week. And as for how long, it's been going on for many months now.
During these episodes, do you often find yourself eating a large amount of food even when you're not physically hungry?

Yes, that's exactly it. A lot of times, this happens after I've already had my supper. My stomach isn't asking for anything at all, I'm not hungry... but I still go back into the pantry or the fridge. I'll just start picking at things, and then it just turns into eating a whole lot of food, even though I didn't need it.
During these episodes, do you tend to eat alone because you feel embarrassed about how much you're eating?

No, not really. I don't purposely go off by myself to eat just to hide it. I mean, sometimes I am alone when it happens, just because of how the day goes, but it's not because I'm trying to sneak away or because I'm embarrassed for people to see me. I just eat where I normally would.

Lack of secretive eating due to embarrassment does not exclude binge eating disorder, as not all associated features are required. This pattern is consistent with Binge Eating Disorder, supporting the previous candidate without need for change.
